column1: # *** ⚠ THIS FILE WAS POLLUTED BY ITS OWN TEST SUITE. FOUND AND FIXED 2026-09-10. ***
# `dice.roll()` logs by DEFAULT -- correct for play, because this file is the
# evidence -- so EVERY `pytest tools/tests` run wrote 31 rows into it. It had been
# doing that for as long as those tests existed. Found while checking whether the
# log was current before a compact: the tail held attack rolls for a giant centipede
# and an orc that no character in this campaign has ever met.
# SCALE: the test rows include 5 "giant centipede attacks AC 9" and 1 "orc attacks
# AC 9" per run. Those markers count 625 and 125, which agree exactly: 125 RUNS,
# about 3,875 rows, in a file of 7,247. MORE THAN HALF THIS FILE IS TEST OUTPUT.
# HOW TO TELL THEM APART: play rows carry a reason that names the day or the
# expedition ("day 69: ..."). Test rows are terse and carry no exped and no turn --
# "morale", "giant centipede attacks AC 9", "F save vs Spell", "wandering check,
# anchor 20", "initiative, party". Some of those strings DO occur in real play, so
# no single grep separates them cleanly; the centipede and orc lines are unique to
# the suite.
# THE LEAK IS CLOSED: tools/tests/conftest.py redirects dice.ROLLS to a scratch file
# for the whole session, and tools/tests/test_no_roll_log_leak.py is the alarm --
# it rolls a die and asserts this file's size did not move.
# THE EXISTING 3,875 ROWS ARE STILL HERE, DELIBERATELY. This log is append-only by
# doctrine and purging it is the player's call, not the DM's. Nothing has been
# deleted.
# Every die rolled, appended automatically by tools/dice.py and tools/combat.py.
# This exists so a disputed sequence can be checked without grepping a 60 MB
# conversation transcript, which is how the encounter log had to be rebuilt
# once. It is an audit trail, not a source of record: nothing reads it back.
# `hidden` marks a roll made in advance and concealed — in practice only the
# wandering-check jitter, which is reported to the player once it fires.
